analysis:
Scope: SSDPrefixCache.evictOldestEntry (patch hunk base 1770-1787 / head 1773-1778) now delegates to SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.evictOldest(index:) with a closure that builds the block URL from the root and calls retireIndexedEntries([url]). The other changes are tests: SSDBlockIndexTests (oldestFirstSnapshot ordering, tie-break, snapshot isolation) and SSDOwnedEntryRetirementTests (Fixture now conforms to SSDEvictableStore, plus new eviction, budget, busy-lease, external-loss, disowned-epoch and bounded-fallback tests). The visible head source (SSDPrefixCache lines 1839-2184) is unchanged context: scanOnDisk, settleDurableDonation and related code.

Security-relevant behavior (T-041, TB-007, A-001):
- The new call path keeps the same guards as before: hasSafeRoot, then retireIndexedEntries, which uses the owned-retirement epoch barrier and the isSafeBlockURL / no-follow checks. The path is still derived from an HMAC tag, never from caller input, so no path traversal or symlink-following surface is added.
- The old code returned 0 when retired.externalChange was set. The new code's equivalent lives in the implementation of SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.evictOldest, which is not in the supplied evidence. The tests assert that external loss stops eviction, that the index keeps its entries, that the epoch is unchanged, and that busy leases are skipped.
- The fallback snapshot is bounded (tests boundedFallback and fallbackSnapshotBoundary), so eviction cannot loop forever when entries are touched or inserted concurrently. This is availability-positive for T-016 and T-060.
- The statsBox eviction counter is only incremented when bytes were freed, as before.
- Eviction does not rotate the cache epoch. This matches the T-041 detection_hint, and the KEK wipe and per-file AES-GCM are untouched.

No regressions found. Residual unverified items: the source of SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.evictOldest and SSDBlockIndex.oldestFirstSnapshot is not supplied, so the production lock discipline (callback without the index lock, snapshot semantics) is only checked through the tests. The new SSDEvictableStore conformance, including reconcileExternalRemovals and performExternalDestructiveChange, is also only exercised through the test fixture. A reviewer with those implementation files should confirm the externalChange early-return and the ownership check match the removed code.
